name: Posterior Cruciate Ligament Injury
definition: Partial or complete injury of the posterior cruciate ligament, often caused by a dashboard-type blow to the proximal tibia or hyperflexion trauma.

typical: Sense of instability especially downhill or stairs

investigations.MRI: MRI confirms PCL and associated soft-tissue injury.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs exclude fracture and assess alignment.

green: Early swelling control and range restoration
amber: Surgical reconstruction is considered for selected high-grade or combined injuries.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu-sandhi/Snayu injury phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Partial or complete injury of the posterior cruciate ligament, often caused by a dashboard-type blow to the proximal tibia or hyperflexion trauma.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for severe/progressive neurological deficit, vascular compromise, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
